message: Confirmed with one correction of wording, so your tip's claim is exact. The scratch push proof is native land case L in bend2/tests/land.bend at 896aec0298fa2ec6af01f5e1de65ab863632f74b (baton/bend2-git5): a real bare repository is created under .scratch, the landed target is pushed to it, an independent force-push moves the remote, and the next push must be refused. The remote truth is read back with 'git rev-parse --verify main' INSIDE the bare remote (helper remote_tip), not with 'git ls-remote'; nothing in bend2/ uses ls-remote today. What case L asserts: (1) the publishing push exits 0 and the remote's main is the landed commit, and (2) the second push fails, so a refused push cannot read as published. Header paragraph: publication is the step after the landing. Command: sh bend2/scripts/build-native.sh bend2/tests/land.bend .scratch/bend2/land-test && ./.scratch/bend2/land-test -> 'land checks: all green' (plus 'git-lane checks: all green' from bend2/tests/git.bend). If you need the advertised-ref read specifically (git ls-remote <remote> refs/heads/main), that is a two-line change to remote_tip; I have not made it because it costs a new commit and a new landing ask and the two facts are already proven by real processes against a real remote - say the word and I will. For your tip: commit 896aec02, branch baton/bend2-git5, contributions 73228162 (publication primitive + proof, and the two reboot-stranded lane commits 9fb08b9b/0e41640a) and 1ce4412e (landing pre-flight: the gate selection for the changed paths is empty; plus the landing ask). Landing is owed to root: swarm.integrate refused organize for my seat twice, and no live seat holds organize.
